content.text:
Fixed. One-line change in `lib/decorate.js:119`:

```js
if (!checkExistence(instance, deps[i]) && !hasInstanceProperty(instance, deps[i])) {
  throw new FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY(deps[i])
}
```

`checkDependencies` now falls back to `hasInstanceProperty` — the helper #6753 added for constructor-assigned properties — so `body`, `id`, `params`, `query`, `log`, `raw` (Request) and `raw`, `request`, `log` (Reply) are accepted as dependencies, matching what `hasRequestDecorator`/`hasReplyDecorator` and the `FST_ERR_DEC_ALREADY_PRESENT` guard already report. Ordering keeps the common path untouched: `checkExistence` short-circuits for ordinary decorators, and `decorate()`'s plain Fastify instance has no `instanceProperties`, so the walk returns `false` at once.

Five tests appended to `test/decorator-instance-properties.test.js` covering the full built-in sets for both constructors, an encapsulated plugin (exercising the `parent` chain), a mixed built-in/user-decorator dependency array, and the regression that unknown names — plus a Reply decorator depending on Request-only `body` — still throw `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY`. All 11 tests in that file pass; I did not run the rest of the suite per your instruction, and the lint command wasn't approved so it's unverified.

Per COMPLEX.md, `lib/decorate.js` isn't listed as a hotspot or in a co-change pair, and the change adds no new symbol or public API surface, so `lib/symbols.js`, `fastify.js` and the type declarations need no matching edit.
